excerpt: Guide to truck accidents on I-16 in Savannah, Georgia, a main Port of Savannah freight route. Covers Port of Savannah freight traffic, construction zone hazards, crash statistics, and Georgia truck accident law (O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33).
keyTakeaways: I-16 is a main truck route for Port of Savannah freight, and the port handles 14,000 to 16,000 truck moves a day (Georgia Ports Authority). Federal crash data recorded 66 deaths on I-16 statewide from 2020 through 2024. The corridor features active GDOT construction zones, two-lane rural stretches, and relentless tractor-trailer volume. Georgia's truck fatalities rose 81% from 2013 to 2023 (142 to 257). You have 2 years to file an injury claim (O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33) and can recover damages if less than 50% at fault.

faqs.question: Why is I-16 dangerous for truck crashes?
faqs.answer: I-16 is a main truck route for Port of Savannah freight, and the port handles 14,000 to 16,000 truck moves a day, Monday through Friday (Georgia Ports Authority). Heavy tractor-trailer traffic, GDOT construction at the I-16/I-95 interchange, long rural stretches with two lanes in each direction and high speeds all add risk. Federal crash data recorded 61 fatal crashes and 66 deaths on I-16 across Georgia from 2020 through 2024 (NHTSA Fatality Analysis Reporting System).

faqs.question: How does Port of Savannah traffic affect I-16 truck accidents?
faqs.answer: The Port of Savannah processed 5.9 million TEUs in 2023, and every container leaving by road travels I-16 westbound. This creates enormous truck volume on tight delivery schedules, with some drivers unfamiliar with local conditions. The port's $1.9 billion expansion will increase truck lanes from 53 to 100 by 2030, further increasing freight volume on I-16.

faqs.question: Are truck crashes more dangerous in construction zones on I-16?
faqs.answer: Yes. GDOT is actively reconstructing the I-16/I-95 interchange and widening I-16 through Chatham County. Construction zones eliminate escape routes with concrete barriers, narrow lanes to leave minimal clearance, and create speed differentials. A truck crash in a construction zone often produces more severe injuries because there is nowhere to go.

faqs.question: Who is liable for an I-16 truck accident?
faqs.answer: Multiple parties may share liability: the truck driver (fatigue, distraction, impairment), the trucking company (negligent hiring, HOS pressure, poor maintenance), the cargo shipper (overweight or improperly loaded containers from the port), the truck or parts manufacturer (defective brakes, tires), and in construction zone crashes, potentially the construction contractor or GDOT.

faqs.question: What evidence should I collect at an I-16 truck accident scene?
faqs.answer: Photograph the truck's company name and USDOT number (displayed on the cab door), trailer number, cargo type, all vehicle damage, mile markers, road conditions, and construction zone signage. Note whether the truck appeared to be a port container truck, tanker, flatbed, or other type. This information helps identify all liable parties and applicable insurance policies.
